name: The Great Drought
region: Central & North India (UP, Bihar, Rajasthan, MP)
historicalContext: Two consecutive monsoon failures. Food grain production fell 20%. India imported 10 million tonnes under PL-480. Near-famine in Bihar. Catalyzed the Green Revolution.

availableCrops.name: Bajra (Pearl Millet)
availableCrops.historicalNote: Primary Kharif crop of Rajasthan & UP. Thrives in sandy, shallow soils with minimal water. Saved millions during the drought.

availableCrops.name: Ragi (Finger Millet)
availableCrops.historicalNote: Grown in dryland Bihar & MP. Highest calcium content of any cereal. Could grow where nothing else survived.

availableCrops.name: Jowar (Sorghum)
availableCrops.historicalNote: Major food crop of semi-arid Central India. Dual-purpose: grain for humans, stalks as cattle fodder.

availableCrops.name: Desi Wheat (Local Variety)
availableCrops.historicalNote: Traditional wheat varieties grown pre-Green Revolution. Moderate yield but needed more water than millets.

availableCrops.name: Hybrid Paddy (IR-8 Prototype)
availableCrops.historicalNote: Early HYV rice being trialed. Massive yield under perfect irrigation but catastrophic failure without water. The 1965 drought proved this vulnerability.

availableCrops.name: Sugarcane
availableCrops.historicalNote: Water-guzzling cash crop. In 1965, sugarcane fields dried to husks while millet farmers survived. The ultimate gamble.

disaster.name: Monsoon Failure — महा सूखा
disaster.triggerDescription: The skies refuse to break. IMD records -60% rainfall. Wells run dry. Dust storms sweep the plains.

specialRules: Crops with droughtTolerance > 0.70 survive at 45% yield
Aquifer recharge drops to 30% of normal
Food consumption increases 20% (heat stress on family)
